Thus then vve {{ls}}ee that by al meanes the old vulgar Latin tran{{ls}}lation is approued good, and better then the Greeke text it {{ls}}elf, and that there is no cau{{ls}}e vvhy it {{ls}}hould giue place to any other text,copies, or readings. Marie if there be any faultes euidently crept in by tho{{ls}}e that heretofore wrote or copied out the Scriptures (as there be {{ls}}ome) them vve graunt no le{{ls}}{{ls}}e, then vve vvould graunt faultes novv a daies committed by the Printer, and they are exactly noted of Catholike vvriters, namely in al Plantins Bibles {{ls}}et forth by the Diuines {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Seß.'' 4.}}of Louan: and the holy Councel of Trent vvilleth that the vulgar Latin text be in {{ls}}uch pointes throughly mended, & {{ls}}o to be mo{{ls}}t authentical. Such faultes are the{{ls}}e, ''In fide,'' for, ''in fine: Præ{{ls}}cientiam,'' for, ''præ{{ls}}entiam: Su{{ls}}cipiens,'' for, ''Su{{ls}}piciens:'' and {{ls}}uch like very rare. vvhich are euident corruptions made by the copi{{ls}}tes, or grovven by the {{ls}}imilitude of vvordes. The{{ls}}e being taken avvay, vvhich are no part of tho{{ls}}e corruptions and differences before talked of, vve tran{{ls}}late that text vvhich is mo{{ls}}t {{ls}}incere, and in our opinion and as vve haue proued, incorrupt. The Aduer{{ls}}aries contrarie tran{{ls}}late that text, vvhich them {{ls}}elues confe{{ls}}{{ls}}e both by their vvritings and doings,to be corrupt in a number of places,& more corrupt then our vulgar Latin, as is before declared.

{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Caluini{{ls}}ts confe{{ls}}{{ls}}ing the Greeke to be mo{{ls}}t corrupt, yet tran{{ls}}late that only, and hold that only for authentical Scripture.}}And if vve vvould here {{ls}}tand to recite the places in the Greeke vvhich Beza pronounceth to be corrupted, vve {{ls}}hould make the Reader to vvonder, hovv they can either {{ls}}o plead othervvi{{ls}}e for the Greeke text, as though there vvere no other truth of the nevv Te{{ls}}tament but that: or hovv they tran{{ls}}late onely that (to deface, as they thinke, the old vulgar Latin) vvhich them {{ls}}elues {{ls}}o {{ls}}hamfully di{{ls}}grace, more then the vulgar Latin, inuenting corruptions vvhere none are, nor can be, in {{ls}}uch vniuer{{ls}}al con{{ls}}ent of al both Greeke and Latin copies. For example, ''Mat.'' 10. ''The fir{{ls}}t Simon, Vvho is called Peter.'' I thinke * {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=* ''In Annot. No. Te{{ls}}t. an.'' 1556.}}({{ls}}aith Beza) this vvord πρῶτος, ''fir{{ls}}t, hath been added to the text of {{ls}}ome that vvould e{{ls}}tabli{{ls}}h Peters Primacie. Againe Luc.'' 22. ''Figures vvhich they made, to adore them.'' It may be {{ls}}u{{ls}}pected ({{ls}}aith he) that the{{ls}}e vvordes, as many other, haue crept by corruption into the text out of the margent. ''v.'' 42. ὃ ἐστι κοδράντης, ''Vvhich is a farthing:'' and ''Act.'' 8. ''v.'' 26. αὕτη ἐστιν ἔρημος, ''This is de{{ls}}ert.'' and ''Act.'' 7. ''v.'' 16 the name of Abraham, & {{ls}}uch like.
